subject.title: Embedded runner: freshly streamed thinking signatures intermittently invalid on replay (Anthropic); recovery wrapper never fires because error text is genericized

question: Should OpenClaw stop replaying completed-turn Anthropic signed-thinking blocks for Claude 4-family models now, or keep the current provider-owned replay default and rely only on recovery until compatibility proof is stronger?
rationale: The remaining change is not a simple local bug patch: current policy deliberately preserves Claude 4-family thinking blocks, and changing that default has provider replay, cache, auth-provider, and message-delivery compatibility consequences.

options.title: Choose a prevention PR
options.body: Review and land a narrow prevention PR such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99383 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100149 after upgrade/live proof covers active tool turns and Claude 4 replay behavior.

options.title: Recovery-only for now
options.body: Keep current signed-thinking replay semantics and rely on the merged recovery wrapper, accepting that prevention remains open for deployments that still hit first-attempt 400s.

options.title: Split the tracker
options.body: Move remaining prevention to the narrower open issue and keep this broad thread only as historical evidence once a maintainer names the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Choose a prevention PR
recommendation.body: Review and land a narrow prevention PR such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99383 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100149 after upgrade/live proof covers active tool turns and Claude 4 replay behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Merged the async recovery fix and is the clearest available history-backed owner for deciding whether the remaining replay-policy change is safe to land.
